question: Do small changes to the Ising model preserve its critical large-scale behavior?
idea: The manuscript claims that certain sufficiently weak, symmetry-preserving extra interactions leave the critical spin and energy limits unchanged. Under the stated conditions, interfaces have the same limiting random-curve law too. A disorder result also requires weak bounded independent randomness; arbitrary perturbations are not covered.
why: The study of randomness and large collections of interacting parts. It connects individual random events with collective patterns.

glossary.meaning: A model in which many sites carry one of two states and interact with one another.
The mathematics of uncertainty and random behavior.

exactClaim: Weak finite-range square-symmetric even multispin perturbations of the square-lattice Ising model preserve critical bulk spin and energy limits; weak square-symmetric contour interactions also yield chordal SLE3 interface limits. With sufficiently weak iid bond disorder of any fixed bounded nondegenerate mean-zero law, critical spin interfaces converge to the same law in probability over environments. )
reviewStatus: assistant-authored from source summary; not mathematically reviewed
scope: Family-level introduction based on the pinned catalogue summary. Summarizes manuscript claims; not an independent proof review.
